A000670.name: Fubini numbers: number of preferential arrangements of n labeled elements; or number of weak orders on n labeled elements; or number of ordered partitions of [n].
A000670.author: _N. J. A. Sloane_
A000670.conjecture: Conjecture: Let k be a positive integer. The sequence obtained by reducing a(n) modulo k is eventually periodic with the period dividing phi(k) = A000010(k). For example, modulo 16 we obtain the sequence [1, 1, 3, 13, 11, 13, 11, 13, 11, 13, ...], with an apparent period of 2 beginning at a(4). Cf. A354242.

A002050.name: Number of simplices in barycentric subdivision of n-simplex.
A002050.author: _N. J. A. Sloane_
A002050.conjecture: Conjecture: Let k be a positive integer. The sequence obtained by reducing a(n) modulo k is eventually periodic with the period dividing phi(k) = A000010(k). For example, modulo 9 we obtain the sequence [0, 1, 5, 7, 5, 1, 5, 4, 5, 7, 5, 1, 5, 4, 5, 7, 5, 1, 5, 4, 5, 7, 5, ...], with an apparent period of 6 = phi(9) beginning at a(5). - _Peter Bala_, Aug 03 2023

A004123.name: Number of generalized weak orders on n points.
A004123.author: _N. J. A. Sloane_
A004123.conjecture: Conjecture: Let k be a positive integer. The sequence obtained by reducing a(n) modulo k is eventually periodic with the period dividing phi(k) = A000010(k). For example, modulo 7 we obtain the sequence [1, 2, 3, 4, 2, 0, 0, 2, 3, 4, 2, 0, 0, 2, 3, 4, 2, 0, 0, ...] with an apparent period of 6 = phi(7) starting at a(2). Cf. A000670.

A006531.name: Semiorders on n elements.
A006531.author: _N. J. A. Sloane_
A006531.conjecture: Conjecture: for fixed k = 1,2,..., the sequence a(n) (mod k) is eventually periodic with the exact period dividing phi(k), where phi(k) is Euler's totient function A000010. For example, modulo 10 the sequence becomes (1, 1, 3, 9, 3, 1, 3, 9, 3, ...) with an apparent period 1, 3, 9, 3 of length 4 = phi(10) beginning at a(1). (End)
A006531.egf: E.g.f.: C(1-exp(-x)), where C(x) = (1 - sqrt(1 - 4*x)) / (2*x) is the ordinary g.f. for the Catalan numbers A000108. [corrected by _Joel B. Lewis_, Mar 29 2011]

A052895.name: Expansion of e.g.f. (1/2)/(exp(x) - 1) * (1 - (5 - 4*exp(x))^(1/2)).
A052895.author: _INRIA Encyclopedia of Combinatorial Structures_, Jan 25 2000
A052895.conjecture: Conjecture: for fixed k = 1,2,..., the sequence a(n) (mod k) is eventually periodic with the exact period dividing phi(k), where phi(k) is the Euler totient function A000010. For example, modulo 10 the sequence becomes (1, 1, 5, 3, 5, 1, 5, 3, 5, ...), with an apparent period 1, 5, 3, 5 of length 4 = phi(10) beginning at a(1). (End)

A064618.name: Stirling transform of (n!)^2.
A064618.author: _Karol A. Penson_, Sep 26 2001
A064618.conjecture: Conjecture: for fixed k = 1,2,..., the sequence a(n) (mod k) is eventually periodic with the exact period dividing phi(k), where phi(k) is the Euler totient function A000010. For example, modulo 10 the sequence becomes (1, 1, 5, 9, 1, 1, 5, 9, ...), with an apparent period 1, 1, 5, 9 of length 4 = phi(10) beginning at a(0). - _Peter Bala_, Jan 15 2018

A080253.name: a(n) is the number of elements in the Coxeter complex of type B_n (or C_n).
A080253.author: _Paul Boddington_ and _Tim Honeywill_, Feb 10 2003
A080253.conjecture: Conjecture: Let k be a positive integer. The sequence obtained by reducing a(n) modulo k is eventually periodic with the period dividing phi(k) = A000010(k). For example, modulo 7 we obtain the sequence [1, 3, 3, 0, 3, 4, 0, 3, 3, 0, 3, 4, 0, 3, 3, 0, 3, 4, 0, ...], with an apparent period of 6 = phi(7) beginning at a(1). Cf. A000670. - _Peter Bala_, Dec 31 2025
A080253.egf: E.g.f.: exp(x)/(2-exp(2*x)). - Antonio G. Astudillo (afg_astudillo(AT)hotmail.com), Feb 14 2003

A162314.name: Row sums of A162313.

A167137.name: E.g.f.: P(exp(x)-1) where P(x) is the g.f. of the partition numbers (A000041).
A167137.author: _Paul D. Hanna_, Nov 03 2009

A259533.name: Number of restricted barred preferential arrangements of an n-set having 3 bars in which 3 fixed sections are restricted sections and 1 section is a free section.

A301921.name: Expansion of e.g.f. 1/(1 - (exp(x) - 1)/(1 - (exp(x) - 1)^2/(1 - (exp(x) - 1)^3/(1 - ...)))), a continued fraction.
A301921.author: _Ilya Gutkovskiy_, Jun 19 2018
A301921.conjecture: Conjecture: Let k be a positive integer. The sequence obtained by reducing a(n) modulo k is eventually periodic with the period dividing phi(k) = A000010(k). For example, modulo 9 we obtain the sequence [0, 1, 3, 1, 6, 4, 0, 7, 3, 1, 6, 4, 0, 7, 3, 1, 6, 4, 0, 7, ...] with an apparent period of 6 = phi(9) beginning at n = 2. Cf. A004123. (End)
A301921.egf: Expansion of e.g.f. 1/(1 - (exp(x) - 1)/(1 - (exp(x) - 1)^2/(1 - (exp(x) - 1)^3/(1 - ...)))), a continued fraction.

A316142.name: Expansion of e.g.f. Product_{k>=1} (1 + (exp(x)-1)^k)^2.

For example, modulo 7 we obtain the sequence [1, 2, 1, 0, 0, 2, 2, 2, 1, 0, 0, 2, 2, 2, 1, 0, 0, 2, 2, ...], with a preperiod of length 1 and an apparent period thereafter of 6 = phi(7). - _Peter Bala_, Mar 03 2023

A316144.name: Expansion of e.g.f. Product_{k>=1} ((1 + (exp(x)-1)^k) / (1 - (exp(x)-1)^k))^2.

A320352.name: Expansion of e.g.f. (exp(x) - 1)/(exp(x) - exp(2*x) + 1).
